newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast signs agricultural sector loan deal.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast signs agricultural sector loan deal.

text.p: Ivory Coast on Tuesday underlined its commitment to foreign debt reduction after signing an agricultural sector loan deal with the African Development Bank.

"It (the loan) will allow us to deal with treasury difficulties encountered in 1996 and which will most likely continue into 1997 given the weight of external debt," Finanace Minister N'Goran Niamien said.

AfDB president Omar Kabbaj said the loan, for around 11.4 billion CFA francs, took overall the bank's lending to Ivory Coast to $1.3 million. About $65 million of that was on concessional terms offered by the bank's soft-loan arm, the African Development Fund.
Interest rate charges for the latest loan had been set at less than one percent, he told a news conference.
Ivory Coast would aim to reduce debt servicing levels and cut a budgetary deficit of two percent of GDP, said Niamen.
An International Monetary Fund spokesman said the loan had been agreed earlier but had not been drawn down because of lack of ADF reserves after other clients defaulted.
Recent ADB reorganisations had made disbursements possible.

"It is aimed at relaunching quality growth and had to address the agricultural sector which had then been neglected with low world prices," resident IMF official Pierre van den Boogaerde told Reuters in an interview before the signature.
The ADB said at the signing that lending to Ivory Coast's private sector could increase in 1996-98 with priority given to agricultural, social and public facility projects.
